characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Supra 55 FEG-SEM equipped with EDS and Nordley EBSD detectors (Oxford); step size 120 nm / 250 nm on ~100×100 μm² to ~200×200 μm² areas; analyzed with TSL-OIM software
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fine equiaxed randomly oriented recrystallized austenite grains; nearly uniform red FCC matrix with sparse fine blue B2 particles; KAM almost uniformly low (dark blue) indicating low stored strain.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Colored IPF (austenite), phase contrast, and KAM maps acquired on HR+CR+1023 K samples
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize microstructure, phase contrast and stored strain (KAM) of 28Mn0Ni at 1023 K

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, constant cross-head speed 0.5 mm min^-1 (initial strain rate ~3×10^-4 s^-1), ASTM E8M flat specimens (gauge length 30 mm, width 6 mm, thickness 4–5 mm)
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate strength and ductility of 28Mn0Ni in HR+CR+1023 K condition

interfaces.interface_notes: In the Ni-free alloy intragranular B2 particles are inferred not to pin newly recrystallized grains but to delay overall recovery; nucleation of recrystallized grains occurs along γ/γ boundaries and γ/B2 interfaces.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Upon heat treatment secondary κ-carbide and B2 phases precipitate and their fraction decreases with increasing temperature; at 1023 K the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni alloy undergoes complete recrystallization of austenite. (XRD-confirmed κ-carbide/B2 formation at 973 K decreasing at higher temperature.)
interfaces.slip_behavior: Austenite deforms predominantly by planar slip; in recrystallized austenite, planar slip activity followed by dynamic slip band refinement. (General behaviour reported for the LDS alloys including 28Mn0Ni.)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sound portion of the 30 kg vacuum induction melted ingot homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h prior to hot rolling.
Hot rolled at 1323 K; final thickness of hot rolled plate was about 13 mm. This condition is referred to as HR.
Samples cut from hot-rolled plates were cold rolled at room temperature to ~50% reduction in thickness (~6 mm thick sheets) in several passes. Denoted HR+CR.
Cold rolled sheet heat treated at 1023 K for 1 h followed by water quenching; sample referred to by heat treatment temperature (HR+CR+1023 K).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tests triplicated; average of three readings reported
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Flat tensile specimen, gauge length 30 mm, width 6 mm, thickness 4–5 mm

microstructure_counts.recrystallized_fraction_of_austenite: between 0.8 and 1.0 (at the intermediate temperature ~1023 K, Fig. 5a)

defects.lattice_distortion: KAM map of 28Mn0Ni at 1023 K is almost uniformly dark blue (near-minimum misorientation) with only a few isolated green/yellow-green spots
defects.type: low stored strain / low local misorientation

phases_present.morphology: fine, equiaxed, randomly oriented recrystallized grains (multi-coloured IPF)
sparse fine blue particles dispersed within the FCC matrix (phase map)

precipitates.type: B2 (FeAl-based ordered phase; general heat-treated feature: fine intragranular B2 50–200 nm and coarser intergranular B2 0.5–1.5 μm)

structures.overall_structure: 28Mn0Ni (Fe–28Mn–9Al-0.9C, Ni-free) in HR+CR+1023 K condition: nearly single-phase austenitic (FCC) matrix with a low fraction of fine secondary B2 particles. OIM-EBSD phase map is essentially uniform red (FCC) with sparse fine blue (B2) particles dispersed within grains. The cold rolled microstructure transformed from partial recrystallization at 973 K to complete recrystallization at 1023 K, giving fine equiaxed, randomly oriented recrystallized austenite grains with low stored strain.

unmapped_findings: For the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni (Fe–28Mn–9Al-0.9C) alloy in HR+CR+1023 K, the cold rolled microstructure transformed from partial recrystallization at 973 K to complete recrystallization at 1023 K; the fraction of recrystallized austenite at ~1023 K (intermediate data point) lies between 0.8 and 1.0 (Fig. 5a).

A 50 K increase in heat treatment temperature (973 K → 1023 K) for 28Mn0Ni accelerated the recrystallization kinetics but caused a drastic reduction in strength (from YS ~900 MPa / 23% elongation at 973 K to YS 732 MPa / 36% elongation at 1023 K) (b0079).

No Vickers hardness data point is reported explicitly for 28Mn0Ni at 1023 K; Fig. 8b plots hardness against heat treatment temperature at 873, 973, 1073, 1173 and 1273 K only. For 28Mn0Ni hardness decreases monotonically with heat treatment temperature.

XRD patterns (Fig. 2a) for 28Mn0Ni were reported only for HR+CR, HR+CR+973 K and HR+CR+1173 K conditions; no XRD trace at 1023 K is given. At 973 K additional peaks of κ-carbide and B2 appear, whereas at 1173 K only γ peaks remain.

TEM analysis for 28Mn0Ni was reported at 973 K (mixed recrystallized/deformed austenite with intragranular κ-carbides 10–60 nm and intergranular B2) and at 1173 K (precipitate-free); no TEM data specific to the 1023 K condition is provided.

In tensile tests the 28Mn0Ni alloy in HR+CR+1023 K exhibited significant ductility (36 ± 2 %) in contrast to the 15Mn5Ni alloy which was brittle (<1%) under the same condition; post-tensile fractography specific to 28Mn0Ni was reported for the 1023 K condition showing ductile dimple rupture.
